display.title: B'chol Dor Vador: Seeing Ourselves Leave Mitzrayim
display.summary_short: A Chol HaMoed Pesach talk on why the freedom from Mitzrayim is our own freedom today, with a dramatized skit about B'chol Dor Vador and the lead-in to a Yom Tov march.
display.summary_long: A Pesach segment from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, recorded during Chol HaMoed. Uncle Yossi reviews why we hold a Seder, eat matzah and maror, drink wine and lean: as the Haggadah says, had Hashem not taken our fathers out of Mitzrayim, we would still be slaves, so those miracles are our miracles and that freedom is ours. One of the Twelve Pesukim, B'chol Dor Vador, teaches that in every generation each person must see himself as if he personally left Mitzrayim. Then comes a short dramatized skit: two children in pajamas dream they are in 'Mitzvah Stone National Park', free a deer stuck in a bush, and remember how Hashem freed us from Egypt and that we should thank Him every day. The clip ends as Uncle Yossi introduces the Hakochainik march, the Yom Tov song 'Mi'Mitzrayim Ge'altanu', explaining its words from the Haggadah; the song itself is not included.
display.lesson: The Exodus is our own freedom: each of us should feel as if we left Mitzrayim today, and thank Hashem with joy.
